Pla pao is `a popular Thai dish made of a whole fish—usually tilapia or snapper—stuffed with herbs, coated in a thick salt crust, and grilled over charcoal` . It is typically served with fresh vegetables, rice noodles, and a spicy garlic-lime chili dipping sauce.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ui1v1nV_E-E&t=18) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ui1v1nV_E-E&t=18)[[2]](https://www.tumblr.com/fuckyeahgrilling/96459326441/authentic-thai-grilled-fish-recipe-pla-pao)[[3]](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/authentic-thai-grilled-fish-recipe-pla-pao--278941770649858035/)[[4]](https://www.andy-cooks.com/blogs/recipes/thai-whole-grilled-snapper-pla-pao)[[5]](https://hungryinthailand.com/pla-pao/)

Key Ingredients

- **Fish:** Whole fresh tilapia or sea bass, gutted through the gills with scales left intact to protect the meat.
- **Stuffing:** Stalks of bruised lemongrass and fresh kaffir lime leaves.
- **Salt Crust:** Coarse salt mixed with a small amount of all-purpose flour and water to help it stick like wet sand.
- **Dipping Sauce:** Thai bird chilies, garlic, lime juice, fish sauce, and a touch of sugar pounded in a mortar.[](https://www.andy-cooks.com/blogs/recipes/thai-whole-grilled-snapper-pla-pao) [[1]](https://theculturecook.com/recipe-thai-grilled-fish-recipe-pla-pao.html)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TuZ_0A97xRU)

How It Is Served and Eaten

- **Style:** Often enjoyed as a street food or part of an Isaan meal alongside sticky rice, som tam (papaya salad), and larb.
- **Miang Style:** Diners frequently flake the moist fish meat off the bone and wrap small portions inside fresh salad leaves or cabbage with rice noodles and the spicy seafood sauce.[](https://www.eatingthaifood.com/thai-grilled-fish-recipe-pla-pao/) [[1]](https://www.eatingthaifood.com/thai-grilled-fish-recipe-pla-pao/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/YOZlNHHOnIM)
